title: Calf muscles: gastrocnemius and soleus
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs; 14.3; 16.4; 20.2

main.t: The gastrocnemius and soleus form the calf and pull on the calcaneal tendon to point the foot down.

simpler.t: The calf muscles lift your heel so you can stand on tiptoe and push off when walking.

deeper.t: They lie in the superficial posterior compartment of the leg and help keep us upright.

facts.t: The gastrocnemius is the most superficial and visible muscle of the calf; the wide, flat soleus lies deep to it.
Both insert through the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon into the calcaneus.

simpler.t: They form the bulge at the back of your lower leg, ending in the tendon above your heel.

deeper.t: The small plantaris runs obliquely between them to the same tendon.

items.name: Gastrocnemius
items.t: Two heads from the medial and lateral condyles of the femur.

items.name: Soleus
items.t: Wide and flat, from the upper tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane.

items.name: Calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
items.t: A strong tendon into the calcaneus, shared by the superficial calf muscles.

items.name: Plantaris
items.t: A small muscle between the two. Some people have two; about 7 percent of cadavers have none.

simpler.t: Two big muscles, one tendon to the heel.

deeper.t: Surgeons use the plantaris tendon in tendon transplants and ligament repairs.

facts.t: Pulling the heel up, they plantar flex the foot, as in jumping or tapping the foot.
The gastrocnemius crosses the knee, so it also helps flex the leg.
The soleus, crossing the ankle only, helps maintain posture while walking.

simpler.t: They push the front of the foot down and lift the heel.

items.name: Calcaneus
items.t: The heel bone, where the calcaneal tendon inserts.

items.name: Tibialis anterior
items.t: At the front of the leg. It dorsiflexes the foot, opposing the calf.

items.name: Veins of the leg
items.t: Contracting leg muscles squeeze nearby veins, pushing blood towards the heart.

items.name: Deep posterior muscles
items.t: Popliteus, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus and tibialis posterior lie beneath.

items.name: Tibial nerve
items.t: One of the two nerves in the sciatic nerve. It supplies the back of the leg.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). That the tibial nerve supplies the calf muscles.

simpler.t: They pull on the heel and work against the muscles at the front of the shin.

facts.t: They develop from general mesoderm, like all limb muscles.
The plantaris varies most: some people have two, and about 7 percent of cadavers have none.

items.injury: Tapping the calcaneal tendon with a reflex hammer.
items.damaged: The ankle reflex of the gastrocnemius and soleus.
items.cannotDo: Show a normal ankle reflex if the reflex arc is broken.
items.why: Stretch of the muscle excites its own motor neurons through the spinal cord.

items.injury: A sudden push-off that ruptures the calcaneal tendon.
items.cannotDo: Stand on tiptoe on that leg or push off when walking.
items.why: The calf muscles can no longer pull on the calcaneus.
items.check: Not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–17, 19–23 and 25). Rupture of the calcaneal tendon and its signs.

items.q: Explain how walking helps blood return from the legs.
model: Leg muscles, including the calf, contract during walking.
The veins’ one-way valves let blood move only upwards.
So the skeletal muscle pump moves blood towards the heart.

items.q: Compare the gastrocnemius and the soleus.
model: Both plantar flex the foot through the calcaneal tendon.
The gastrocnemius arises from the femur and crosses the knee.
So it also flexes the leg; the soleus does not.
The soleus lies deep and helps posture while walking.

items.q: Predict what happens to the calf muscles when you step on a tack.
model: Pain fibres excite the motor neurons of the tibialis anterior.
An interneuron inhibits the gastrocnemius and soleus.
Plantar flexion stops, so the foot lifts off the tack.

check.stem: Which calf muscle also flexes the knee?
check.why: The gastrocnemius arises from the femoral condyles, so it crosses and flexes the knee.

check.stem: Where does the calcaneal tendon insert?
check.why: It inserts into the calcaneal bone of the ankle.

check.stem: Which muscle lies deep to the gastrocnemius?
check.why: Deep to the gastrocnemius is the wide, flat soleus.
